# Get proximity matrix of an ranger object

Random forest proximities between the observations in `x` and `y`,
converted to the distance \\\sqrt{1 - p}\\ by default.

## Usage

``` r
proximity_distance(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  rfObject,
  as_dist = TRUE,
  type = c("original", "oob", "rfgap")
)
```

## Arguments

- x:

  a new dataset. For `type = "oob"` and `"rfgap"`: the training data of
  `rfObject`.

- y:

  a second new dataset (Default: NULL)

- rfObject:

  `ranger` object

- as_dist:

  Bool, convert proximity \\p\\ to the distance \\\sqrt{1 - p}\\.

- type:

  proximity type: `"original"` (default), `"oob"` or `"rfgap"`.

## Value

For `type = "original"`: a `dist` object (if `y` is `NULL`) or a matrix
with pairwise proximities (or distances, see `as_dist`) of observations
in x (rows) vs y (columns). For the other types always a matrix; RF-GAP
proximities are not symmetric.

## Details

Three types of proximity are available:

- `"original"`:

  Breiman's proximity: the share of trees in which two observations
  share a terminal node. In-sample proximities are inflated because
  observations are counted in the trees they were trained on.

- `"oob"`:

  Only trees in which the training observation (and, for in-sample
  queries, the query) is out-of-bag are used.

- `"rfgap"`:

  RF-GAP proximities (Rhodes, Cutler & Moon, 2023): for query \\q\\ and
  training observation \\j\\, \\p(q, j) = \frac{1}{\|S_q\|} \sum\_{t \in
  S_q} c_j(t) 1\[j \in leaf_t(q)\] / \|M_q(t)\|\\, where \\S_q\\ are the
  trees in which \\q\\ is out-of-bag (all trees for new data),
  \\c_j(t)\\ is the in-bag count of \\j\\ and \\\|M_q(t)\|\\ the total
  in-bag count in \\q\\'s leaf. For each query the proximities sum to 1,
  and the proximity-weighted average of the training outcomes reproduces
  the forest's (out-of-bag) prediction for regression forests.

`"oob"` and `"rfgap"` need the in-bag counts: fit the forest with
`keep.inbag = TRUE` and pass the forest's training data as `x` (same
rows, same order). If `y` is `NULL`, the training data is also used as
query (in-sample proximities).

## References

Rhodes, J. S., Cutler, A. and Moon, K. R. (2023). Geometry- and
Accuracy-Preserving Random Forest Proximities. IEEE Transactions on
Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 45(9), 10947–10959.
[doi:10.1109/TPAMI.2023.3263774](https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAMI.2023.3263774)

## Examples

``` r
# \donttest{
library(ranger)
rf <- ranger(Species ~ ., data = iris, num.trees = 5, write.forest = TRUE)
proximity_distance(x = iris[, -5], rfObject = rf)

set.seed(1234L)
learn <- sample(1:150, 100)
test <- (1:150)[-learn]
rf <- ranger(Species ~ ., data = iris[learn, ], num.trees = 500,
             write.forest = TRUE, keep.inbag = TRUE)
proximity_distance(x = iris[learn, -5], y = iris[test, -5], rfObject = rf)
```
